claim_boundary: Summary record of three same-day VisDrone-only checks: the highres detector pilot's accuracy gate, its propagation into tracking metrics, and a pretrained-ReID ablation. All on VisDrone2019-DET-val/MOT-val, not Vietnam v5.

part_1_detector_pilot_gate.result: PASS, both metrics moved well past the locked thresholds (ap_small gain 2.2x the required minimum; overall AP improved rather than merely not dropping).

part_2_tracking_propagation.claim_boundary: Same standard-1280/ByteTrack/confidence-0.1 protocol as tracking_visdrone_mot_selected_v1 (the resolution comparison's 1280 row), swapping only the detector checkpoint for the highres pilot's. Not the main 5-class HOTA table's checkpoint.
part_2_tracking_propagation.result: Real improvement across precision, MOTA, ID switches, and fragmentations, with recall essentially flat (not traded away). Confirms the earlier HOTA/DetA decomposition finding that detection quality, not the tracking algorithm, was the bottleneck: a better detector alone improved tracking without touching ByteTrack.

part_3_pretrained_reid_ablation.claim_boundary: Same detector/checkpoint and BoT-SORT thresholds as tracking_visdrone_mot_botsort_reid_v1 (the main 5-class HOTA table's ReID row), swapping only model:auto for a real pretrained embedding (yolo26n-reid.onnx, auto-downloaded via Ultralytics 8.4.115's REID_ASSETS).
part_3_pretrained_reid_ablation.result: NEGATIVE. All three ReID configurations (none, auto, pretrained) cluster within noise (IDF1 0.355-0.358, ID switches 207-209, MOTA 0.004-0.005). A real pretrained appearance embedding does not outperform feature reuse or no ReID at all. Consistent with the prior HOTA/DetA decomposition finding: 60% of objects are mostly_lost, so association quality cannot be the limiting factor when most objects are never consistently detected in the first place.

overall_conclusion: Of the two independent levers tested this session, fixing the detector's train/infer resolution mismatch produced a real, propagating improvement (detection AP up, tracking IDF1/MOTA/precision up); improving the tracker's ReID embedding did not. This further confirms detection quality, not tracking algorithm choice, is this pipeline's dominant lever for both stated goals (small-object detection and tracking).
